Lina (Support): Mariner flagged a sudden increase in 429s from their dedicated pool starting ~08:12 UTC, reporting timeouts and elevated p95 latency. They saw baseline ~120 qps and spikes to ~820 qps during an email campaign.
Marco (SRE): Got it. Do we have the pool id and autoscale policy for Mariner?
Lina (Support): Pool: mariner-prod-01, reserved capacity = 6 GPUs, autoscale policy = cpu_based with max 12, cooldown 5m. Min nodes = 3.
Aisha (EngOps): Hypothesis: min nodes=3 may be too low for warmup + burst; also their request distribution shows lots of short chats (seq len ~40) which kills batching efficiency.
Diego (Customer Success): Customer says they saw ~20% 429s for ~12 minutes, then recovery. They need SLO 99.5 for 95th token latency.
Sam (Oncall): @Aisha can you pull pool metrics (GPU util, queue depth, scaling events) from 08:00–09:00?
Aisha (EngOps): Pulling...
infra-bot: Query executed: metrics.mariner-prod-01.gpu_util (08:00-09:00)
Aisha (EngOps): Quick snapshot: GPU util baseline 62% at 08:00, spiked to 92% at 08:12-08:18. Scale events: one scale-up from 4->6 at 08:14, then another from 6->8 at 08:16. Autoscaler queued event 08:12 but first action at 08:14 due to cooldown and decision window.
Marco (SRE): So autoscale reaction lag ~2m — combined with burst > capacity until additional nodes came alive. That explains 429 window. Any noisy neighbors (heavy batch jobs) during the spike?
Aisha (EngOps): Checking tenant isolation. Found a nightly bulk-embed job from internal tenant 'ingest-harbor' running at 08:10 that used large sequential batches, it was hitting same pool (affinity label match).
Lina (Support): Mariner says they didn't change traffic shape — email campaign time was expected but magnitude was underestimated.
Marco (SRE): Two issues: 1) pool undersized headroom for expected peaks, 2) noisy neighbor (ingest job) scheduled during their peak. Immediate mitigation options: a) add ephemeral burst nodes to pool, b) pin Mariner to its own reserved subset (increase min nodes), c) throttle background jobs or move to different pool.
Diego (Customer Success): Mariner prefers minimal disruption and predictable latency. Recommend reserve additional min nodes so autoscale doesn't need to react for these bursts.
Aisha (EngOps): Quick repro steps to validate fix: 1) increase min nodes to 6, 2) run synthetic load to 900 qps for 15m using our loadgen, 3) confirm p95 token latency under SLO and no 429s. Commands:
```
# increase min nodes
redwoodctl pools update mariner-prod-01 --min-nodes 6
# run load
loadgen --target 900 --duration 900 --model gpt-3x --seq 40 --pool mariner-prod-01
```
Lina (Support): I'll propose that to Mariner. Any quick config we can change to reduce cold-start lag?
Marco (SRE): Reduce cooldown to 2m for that pool temporarily and enable fast-provision flag (prewarm image cache). Also set burst headroom reserve +2 nodes.
Aisha (EngOps): Note: setting min-nodes to 6 + cooldown 2m should avoid the 2m visibility window. But long-term we should separate heavy batch tenants or use affinity rules to prevent noisy neighbors.
Sam (Oncall): Logging runbook link: https://intranet.redwood/runbooks/dedicated-pool-surge. Also filing a postmortem if similar bursts >3x baseline happen again.
Diego (Customer Success): I'll coordinate with Mariner on affinity and committed increase.
Lina (Support): Mariner accepted temporary change. Executing change now.
infra-bot: Action: pools.update request accepted for mariner-prod-01. min_nodes: 3 -> 6. cooldown_seconds: 300 -> 120. prewarm: true
Aisha (EngOps): Kicking off synthetic test now.
Aisha (EngOps): Load test results: sustained 900 qps for 15m, no 429s, p95 token latency improved from 420ms -> 220ms. GPU util peaked at 78%.
Marco (SRE): Nice. Recommend followups: - schedule affinity change to move ingest-harbor off mariner pool during marketing windows - add autoscale policy overlay: burst_threshold 600 qps -> immediately add +2 nodes - update cost estimate and inform billing.
Diego (Customer Success): I'll coordinate with Mariner on affinity and committed increase.
Lina (Support): Closing loop: temporary fix applied, repro validated. Creating a ticket for long-term isolation/billing changes. :white_check_mark:
Sam (Oncall): Marking incident as mitigated. If Mariner sees anything else reopen.
